title: review: G9 fix round 2: executor.start passes the task to pick_executor so cost-based routing runs in production (review T-0310)
spec:
STEP 0: the worktree must contain ad6bdf2 "Route by per-class executor success" over 8a84cfa in git log; never drop them.
Review T-0310 on T-0308 (high): orchestrator/executor.py start() still calls pool.pick_executor("execute", t["complexity"], scores=scores) without task=t, and the expected-cost and success-floor routing only activates when task is given, so the whole G9 feature is dead code outside the unit tests.
Change: executor.start() (and any other production caller of pick_executor for execute tasks, grep the package) passes task=t. Add tests/test_executor.py::test_start_routes_with_task (pick_executor monkeypatched to capture kwargs; assert task is the bus task dict) and keep every existing executor test green. No other change.
acceptance: git log --oneline in the worktree shows ad6bdf2 and 8a84cfa below your commit
grep shows no production pick_executor call for execute tasks without task=
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: codex_available() still calls pick_executor("execute", complexity) without task=. Acceptance criterion 3 requires grep to show no production pick_executor call for execute tasks lacking task=; this line still matches. It also creates a real divergence: pool.codex_available() (used by mcp status, pool.status(), daemon's cooling notice) can say an executor is available via generic scores while executor.start()'s task-aware routing picks a different/no executor for that same task.
